detail.title: UCLA DMA Summer Institute — Net Course
detail.body: Among all the tools, platforms and services, the internet is a canvas for expression. Of data Ideas and feelings. As the instructor for the “Net” course at UCLA’s Design Media Arts Summer Institute (2024–2025), I developed and led an intensive, one-week curriculum introducing students to creative web practices. The course explored the web as both a technical and expressive medium, combining coding fundamentals with design experimentation. Working with students from a wide range of backgrounds, I structured the class to move quickly from foundational concepts into hands-on making. Students created interactive sketches using p5.js and developed personal portfolio websites, often encountering code for the first time and leaving with fully realized, self-directed projects. The course emphasized exploration, iteration, and individual voice—encouraging students to treat the web not just as a tool, but as a space for creative practice. Across both in-person and remote sessions, the result was a diverse body of work that reflected each student’s unique approach to interaction, storytelling, and form.
